svg.title: The Great Plague of London (1665): Out-Parishes, Walled City, Pest Houses and Plague Pits
svg.desc: Zoomed Central London historical GIS map using exact City of London and surrounding London borough boundaries plus the tidal River Thames channel, contrasting the Walled City of London against overcrowded suburban Out-Parishes (St Giles-in-the-Fields, Clerkenwell, Whitechapel, Stepney, Southwark), Tothill Fields and Finsbury Pest Houses, Aldgate and Holywell Mount Mass Plague Pits, and King Charles II's July 1665 flight along the Thames.

svg.text: EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY • PAPER 1 (OPTION 11): MEDICINE IN BRITAIN, c1250–PRESENT
The Great Plague of London (1665): Out-Parishes, Walled City & Quarantine
Stronger civic organisation than 1348 (40-day quarantine, Watchmen, Women Searchers, Pest Houses & Bills of Mortality), yet ~100,000 died.
Why? Continuity in miasma & humoral ideas led to street pitch fires and culling ~240,000 dogs & cats—removing rat predators!
